title: Lewis Cottrell Sr. replaces Bill Matthews in the Piron band
summary: Bocage had Piron hire the elder Cottrell as drummer when Bill Matthews left; he describes his strict, music-reading style.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How did you meet Lewis Cattrall?
Well Lewis was a baby when I was playing with his daddy.
I mean the old man. The old man? Yeah, how did you meet him? Well, that's true.

He's much older than me, you know. Just true playing in the Pierron band. You see, Bill used to play drums with us, you know, Pierron. Bill, what was that? Bill, Matthews, the trombone player? Uh huh. So when Bill left, I don't know why he left, but anyway, I made Pierron get the old man, see, because he was the style drummer we needed in that band, see.
Who taught him to play? Who?
The old man. I told you, a fellow at the theater, yeah. That's right. Yeah. Called Dusty, fine drummer, show man, you know.
What kind of stuff did he play in the Pierron band, Cattrall? Lewis Cattrall. What kind of stuff did he play? Four four rhythms? No, he was strictly, he played by music, you know. Strict by music?

Yeah. And he had a nice touch, you know, he could roll his, roll that snare drum, just perfect, you know. He was wonderful. He never used to use much cymbal playing, though. No, not those days, no. Or wood blocks, did he use much of them? Yeah, he used wood blocks. Tom-toms, did he use any of that?
Not very much. He had them, they didn't do it, by the way too much.
